title: Spec-derived contract conformance across request, error, and auth axes
asA: API consumer trusting the published contract
iWant: every declared endpoint proven conformant on the happy path, the error path, and the auth boundary
soThat: the contract holds by verification, including for the endpoint added yesterday

acceptanceCriteria.description: For every declared operation, a schema-conforming request receives a response that validates against the operation's declared response schema for its status code.
acceptanceCriteria.given: each operation in the generated spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: a valid request is executed against it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response validates against the declared schema for the returned status

acceptanceCriteria.description: For every declared operation accepting a body or parameters, an invalid request receives the declared error envelope with the documented 4xx status.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request violating the input schema is executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is the documented 4xx carrying the problem-details envelope

acceptanceCriteria.description: For every declared operation, the endpoint's x-auth-class is honoured: a caller below the declared class is rejected with 401 or 403 per AC-2106-5.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rejection matches the declared class semantics

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conformance coverage is derived from the generated spec at verification time: an operation added to the surface is covered without anyone registering it manually, and an uncoverable operation fails the run.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the new operation is exercised on all three axes or the run fails naming it

acceptanceCriteria.description: The conformance run is part of the standard verification pipeline and its per-operation results are reported, so contract conformance is visible at every build, not sampled occasionally.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the conformance results appear per operation and a conformance failure fails the pipeline
